name: NY Connects: aging and disability first call
organization: New York State Office for the Aging
description: Free, impartial long-term support information for people of all ages and disabilities.
next_step: Give your county and describe the daily-living need. Ask which local agency should assess it.

name: Find your local New York aging office
organization: New York State Office for the Aging
description: Official local aging office directory, including shared offices and tribal programs.
next_step: Use the office serving your county; ask about meals, transport, home support and caregiver help.
constraints: NYC has one aging office for all five boroughs. Tribal aging contacts are available through the source directory.

name: EISEP: assessment and support at home
organization: New York State Office for the Aging
description: Nonmedical home support, case management and caregiver respite for eligible older adults.
next_step: Ask the local aging office for an EISEP assessment and information about available services and cost sharing.
constraints: Age 60+, assessed daily-living needs and ability to remain safely at home apply. The same services must not be available to the applicant under Medicaid.

name: Medicare counseling: HIICAP
organization: New York State Office for the Aging
description: Free, objective Medicare and related health insurance counseling.
next_step: Ask about coverage, plan questions, EPIC, Medicare Savings Programs and prescription cost assistance.
constraints: For people with Medicare or approaching eligibility and their representatives. Counseling does not guarantee coverage or enrollment.

name: Caregiver support and respite referrals
organization: New York State Office for the Aging
description: Find local support for family and unpaid caregivers.
next_step: Ask your aging office or NY Connects about respite, training and caregiver resources.
constraints: Eligibility, local availability and program costs vary.

name: Long-term-care ombudsman: resident rights
organization: NYS Long Term Care Ombudsman Program
description: Advocacy for residents of nursing homes, assisted living and adult care facilities.
next_step: Give the facility county and ask for the ombudsman serving the resident. Explain the concern and the resident’s wishes.
constraints: For immediate danger, call 911. This edition uses statewide ombudsman routing; local program contacts are not yet mapped.

name: New York veterans benefits advising
description: Free advising for veterans and eligible family members on benefits, claims and appeals.
next_step: Request a benefits screening; ask for a phone or video appointment if travel is difficult.
constraints: Each benefit has separate eligibility requirements. Send private records directly to the advisor.

name: Blind Annuity for qualifying veterans and survivors
description: Monthly state payments for qualifying legally blind wartime veterans and eligible unremarried surviving spouses.
next_step: Ask a veterans benefits advisor to review service, blindness and residency documentation.
constraints: New York residence and domicile, qualifying service and legal blindness rules apply. Blindness need not be service connected. Ask for the current payment rate.

name: Access to Home: disability accessibility modifications
description: Accessibility modifications to a qualifying primary residence through funded local partners.
next_step: Find a funded Local Program Administrator; ask whether it serves your county and accepts resident applications.
constraints: Residents cannot apply directly to HCR. Documented disability, income limits and primary residence conditions apply. Local funding and owner obligations must be checked before work.

name: Access to Home for Heroes: veteran accessibility
description: Accessibility changes and certain emergency repairs for qualifying veterans with disabilities.
next_step: Ask a funded local administrator about intake, veteran status, disability documentation and prior approval.
constraints: Qualifying veteran status, substantial physical limitation, income at or below 120% of area median income and primary residence rules apply. Residents apply through local administrators.

name: RESTORE: emergency home repairs for older homeowners
description: Local partner assistance for qualifying emergency repairs affecting home safety.
next_step: Ask a funded local administrator whether your repair meets the emergency criteria and whether funds are available.
constraints: Age 60+, ownership and occupancy as a primary residence, and household income at or below 100% of area median income apply. Residents cannot apply directly to HCR.

name: TRAID: assistive technology loans and demonstrations
description: Regional device loans and hands-on training for New Yorkers with disabilities.
next_step: Find the regional TRAID center overseeing your county; ask about suitable devices, loans and demonstrations.
constraints: Device or ramp inventory, installation and loan terms require confirmation. A trial is not a grant for permanent equipment.

name: Vision loss: Commission for the Blind referral
description: Statewide referral for assistance for people who are legally blind.
next_step: Ask for your district office and an assessment of vision-related daily-living support.
constraints: Legal blindness and program-specific criteria apply. Ask about the appropriate program rather than assuming a vision diagnosis qualifies.

name: Hearing and speech: New York Relay
description: Telephone communication assistance involving people who are deaf, hard of hearing, deafblind or have a speech disability.
next_step: Dial 711 in New York or use the service instructions for the communication method you need.
constraints: Relay facilitates calls; it does not pay for hearing aids or replace clinical assessment.

name: Disability Rights New York intake
description: Disability rights advocacy and legal assistance subject to intake and program priorities.
next_step: Describe the disability-related rights or access concern to the intake office.
constraints: Public visits are by appointment. Representation is not guaranteed.

name: Nursing Home Transition and Diversion waiver screening
description: Referral to a Regional Resource Development Center for community-living waiver screening.
next_step: Contact the RRDC for the county where the person plans to live. A facility discharge planner can help make the referral.
constraints: Community-based Medicaid eligibility and nursing-home level of care apply. Applicants are age 65+ or age 18–64 with a verified physical disability. Services require RRDC approval; referral does not guarantee enrollment or a ramp.

name: Find a New York Independent Living Center
description: Official directory of disability independent living centers.
next_step: Find a nearby center and confirm county coverage, peer support and advocacy services.
constraints: Local coverage and service availability must be confirmed. This edition has not mapped every center.
